subject: general
question:
Seven boxes A, B, C, D, E, F and G are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order. G is kept third from the bottom. Only two boxes are kept between C and E. A is kept immediately above D. D is kept at one of the positions above G. Only two boxes are kept between B and E. B is not kept at the top-most position.

How many boxes are kept between D and B?
solution:
Given: Seven boxes A, B, C, D, E, F and G are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order. 

1) G is kept third from the bottom. 

2) Only two boxes are kept between B and E.

3) B is not kept at the top-most position.

4) Only two boxes are kept between C and E.
